newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia says all air crash bodies recovered.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia says all air crash bodies recovered.

text.p: Ethiopian Airlines said on Wednesday it had recovered all 125 bodies of people who died in last week's air crash in the Comoro Islands.
The airline's director of public relations told reporters that identification of the bodies was now in progress.

The Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 was hijacked on Saturday as it flew from Addis Ababa to Nairobi. The plane ran out of fuel and crashed into the sea off the Comoros, an archipelago 300 kms (190 miles) east of the African mainland.
In the Comoran capital of Moroni, police were still holding two men suspected of being involved in the hijacking of the plane even though the airline has absolved them of responsibility.
Fifty of the 175 passengers and crew survived.
The two men detained by police were identified by some of the survivors as being two of the three hijackers.
However, the co-pilot, Yonas Mekuria, who was beaten up by the hijackers, said they were not the culprits.
In Addis Ababa, Ethiopian police issued a statement declaring their innocence.
"The Kenyan and the Djibouti nationals who are in custody in Comoro Islands were not involved...," it said. "They are innocent passengers."
